Repo: /home/user/House-building. Review the whole repo as one diff (it is a new project: `git log --oneline` shows every commit; review the current tree, i.e. `git diff --stat $(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD) HEAD` scope). Read first, in this order: docs/CONVENTIONS.md — its golden rule leads your review: **every number on screen is traceable to a named assumption in docs/research/assumptions.md; prices are never hard-coded outside the editable DEFAULTS table; a user override must be what the calculation uses** — then /home/user/Agents/docs/engineering-standards.md sections 1 (input safety) and 7 (core-guarantee tests), then docs/research/assumptions.md, docs/specs/estimator.md, docs/specs/estimator-ui.md.

Files under review: src/calc.js, test/calc.test.mjs, src/page.html, scripts/build.mjs, scripts/smoke.mjs, scripts/log-dispatch.mjs. index.html is generated — check only that it is byte-identical to a fresh `node scripts/build.mjs` (do not edit anything; you are read-only).

Priorities, in order:
1. Real bugs and safety: any way the page shows NaN/Infinity/undefined; any input (form field, override, build-log record text) that reaches innerHTML unescaped (prompts and reports contain < > ` and quotes); any formula in calc.js that disagrees with assumptions.md or with its own traceability comment; any path where an override is accepted but not used; the build script's `export ` stripping producing invalid classic-script (e.g. a line inside a string or comment starting with "export "); idempotency of the build.
2. Three interpretations builder A made — say explicitly whether each is right: (a) ground slab gets slab rebar rate (not zero); (b) the sample house sits ~0.7% above the 8,000-block test floor — is the test brittle, and if so what is the right fix (widen the range, or change the sample) — a recommendation, not a judgment call for you to apply; (c) wastage per material rather than per element, shown read-only in the breakdown table (builder B's deviation 1).
3. Golden-rule drift: any number in page.html that isn't from estimate()/DEFAULTS; any DEFAULTS row missing source/lastChecked/confidence.
4. Test gaps against the standards' "core guarantee": what is the one or two most valuable missing tests?
5. Convention nits last, and only ones that contradict CONVENTIONS.md — not style preferences.

Final message (plain English, under 30 lines): a verdict line (SHIP / FIX FIRST), then findings ranked, each with file:line, why it matters, and the one-line fix; then your answers to 2(a)(b)(c); then the test gaps. Say which findings are golden-rule violations (never negotiable) versus judgment calls.
report:
Verdict: FIX FIRST — one clear golden-rule violation, plus a doc-drift one. Tests 20/20 pass; index.html byte-identical to a fresh build (idempotent).

Findings (most severe first)
1. GOLDEN RULE — 13 of the 30 editable assumptions are accepted as overrides but never used in the maths (calc.js reads only 17 keys; page.html renders an editable input for every key). Dead keys: block_ext_length, block_ext_height, block_ext_thickness, block_int_thickness, mortar_joint_mm, wall_height_default_m, ext_wall_perimeter_factor, ext_wall_thickness_mm, int_wall_thickness_mm, slab_thickness_m, price_omr_cement_bag_50kg, price_omr_sand_m3, price_omr_aggregate_m3. Worse, the page then claims it used them ("Using your own numbers for: Slab thickness"). Fix: wire them in where assumptions.md says they're derived, or render the rest read-only "reference only — not used in v1".
2. GOLDEN RULE (doc side) — the ground slab's steel rate has no matching row in assumptions.md; ≈0.9 t of the 12.9 t is traceable to a code comment only. Fix: add rebar_kg_per_m3_ground_slab (40–60 kg/m³ realistic).
3. Breakdown "Wastage %" column is misleading for rows containing steel (shows concrete wastage only). Fix: show both or relabel "Concrete wastage".
4. Range test has 0.7% headroom (8,053 vs floor 8,000). Recommendation: widen the band in assumptions.md to ~7,000–13,000 and keep the sample house; the golden snapshot catches drift.
5. build.mjs `export ` stripping is unguarded; a future string line starting with "export " would ship a broken page. Fix: `new Function(calcInline)` after stripping, die on parse error.
6. Low — with the m² shortcut ticked, a validation error can flag the hidden room list. Cosmetic.
No XSS found (all text escaped, `<` escaped in inlined JSON). No NaN/Infinity path found.

Builder A's interpretations: (a) ground slab steel — right call, wrong paperwork (needs its own row). (b) test brittle — widen the band, keep the sample. (c) wastage per material — right; it's the golden rule that makes it right; spec line 30 should be amended.

Most valuable missing tests: a sweep over EVERY DEFAULTS key asserting it moves the result or is on a named reference-only list; a build test asserting the inlined calculator parses and index.html has no `export ` at column 0.

Golden-rule violations (non-negotiable): 1 and 2. Judgment calls: 3–6.

Orchestrator decisions: all six accepted. Docs amended (ground-slab rebar row at 50 kg/m³, band widened, used-vs-reference rule, spec amendment). Findings 1, 2, 4 + the key sweep → builder A round 2. Findings 1 (UI side), 3, 5, 6 + the build test → builder B round 2.
outcome: FIX FIRST: 2 golden-rule findings + 4 judgment calls; all accepted; fix round 2 to both builders
